elements.element: Services performed in a professional manner
elements.evidence: Clause warrants only that "the Software and MarketSite.net Service will perform in substantial accordance with the Documentation"; no professional-manner standard appears.

elements.element: Services performed in a workmanlike manner
elements.evidence: No "workmanlike" standard anywhere in the redlined clause; only media are "free from defects in materials and workmanship", which is a media-quality warranty, not a services standard.
"will perform in substantial accordance with the Documentation" — conformance remains qualified by "substantial".
"for a period of twelve (12) months from the date Corio accepts the Software pursuant to Section 3.1 (the \"Warranty Period\")"

elements.element: 90-day services warranty period measured from performance/completion
elements.evidence: Single "Warranty Period" applies to Software and MarketSite.net Service; no separate 90-day services period from performance or completion.
"shall take all commercially reasonable efforts to correct" — an efforts undertaking, not a repair obligation.
"if correction ... is reasonably not possible, replace such Software and MarketSite.net Service free of charge"
"Corio has the right to terminate this Agreement and receive a refund of all prepaid fees"
No compliance-with-laws warranty appears in the clause as rendered.
"free of any willfully introduced computer virus, or any other similar harmful, malicious or hidden program or data"
"for a period of twelve (12) months from the date Corio accepts the Software" (exceeds the 90-day floor)

elements.element: 30-day services warranty period with a services performance warranty
elements.evidence: No services performance warranty (professional/workmanlike or otherwise) and no distinct services period; only "substantial accordance with the Documentation" for Software and the Service.

elements.element: Same remedies (repair, replace, refund) at fallback
elements.evidence: Repair appears only as "commercially reasonable efforts to correct"; replacement and refund are present but the repair leg is not an express repair remedy.

offending_extra_words: from the date Corio accepts the Software pursuant to Section 3.1
reasons: The single edit fixes only the duration: it extends the period to twelve (12) months and deletes the December 31, 1999 sunset. It leaves the preferred level incomplete because there is still no professional-and-workmanlike services warranty, no separate 90-day services period, no compliance-with-laws warranty, and conformance stays qualified as "substantial accordance" rather than express conformance to Documentation.

The repair leg remains "all commercially reasonable efforts to correct", which is an efforts covenant rather than the repair remedy the position requires; replacement and refund of prepaid fees are present.
Fallback also fails on material terms: the software period is satisfied, but there is no services performance warranty or services period at all, so no complete bargain exists at either level.

Minimality fails: the replacement rewrote the whole duration phrase and imported a new acceptance-based trigger cross-referenced to Section 3.1, when changing "sixty (60) days" to "twelve (12) months" and striking the sunset would suffice (official gate: changed-character ratio 0.729 vs 0.600 limit).

Unrelated terms (media warranty, exclusive-remedy statement, benefit-of-Corio limitation, exclusions) are untouched and remain effective; the only intent risk is dependence on the Section 3.1 acceptance mechanic.
